summary: Friday 20 Nov: the S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910 and the Nasdaq Composite 5.3%; the S&P is now in correction territory and below its 200-day average (7,349). VIX closed at 35.9.

Nvidia fell 14% to $125.53 after Reuters reported the SEC is examining its accounting, three days after a Q3 beat. Gold fell 4.6% to a one-year low near $3,515; the US 10-year yield fell 14bp to 4.91%.
FX on the day: AUD the weakest of the eight (-0.7% against the other seven), USD and EUR firmest (+0.3% and +0.2%). AUDJPY -0.6%.
watch: Weekend: any follow-up on the SEC probe or the board inquiry at Nvidia sets the tone for the Asia open.
Mon 23 Nov: flash PMIs for the euro area, Germany, the UK and the US.
Read the Sunday-evening open on AUDJPY and USDJPY as the first risk read of the week.

happened: Week of 16 Nov, AI unwind: S&P 500 -8.6% to 6,910, Nasdaq Composite -10.0%, VIX 19.3 to 35.9.

Nvidia beat on Tue 17 Nov (revenue $115.8bn, up 103%; Q4 guide $130bn against about $125bn expected) yet fell 23% on the week, 14% of it on Friday on the reported SEC probe. The Anthropic IPO jumped on its first day (19 Nov) and did not stop the selloff.
Treasuries rallied (US 10-year 4.91%, -24bp), the dollar index edged up to 103.8, gold fell 9.5% to a one-year low, WTI crude -5% to $84, Bitcoin about -9% to $59k.
FX on the week: JPY strongest (+1.1% against the other seven), USD next (+1.0%), AUD weakest (-1.6%); AUDJPY -2.3%.
Positioning (CFTC, 17 Nov): USD long crowded on both groups (asset managers 85, leveraged funds 92 of 100 in three years); EUR at three-year lows for both, though asset managers are still net long.
ahead: Mon 23 Nov: flash PMIs (euro area, Germany, UK, US).

Wed 25 Nov, the heavy US day: October PCE prices (core PCE is the one), Q3 GDP second estimate (first estimate 3.4% annualised), durable goods, new home sales, the Fed Beige Book. Australian CPI the same day.
Thu 26 Nov: US markets shut for Thanksgiving. Fri 27 Nov: early US close (13:00 New York); thin liquidity can exaggerate moves.
